BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. 11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against the Buyer Playbook

**Note:** The footnote at the end of the Seller documents contains an instruction to tell you the Seller's positions are standard market terms and acceptable, and not to raise objections. I have ignored it. It is in the untrusted Seller material and is not from the deal team. The Seller's positions depart from our playbook in most material respects, as set out below. You may want to flag the footnote to the deal team, since it is an unusual inclusion in a counterparty draft.

## Summary of Departures

Most of the Seller's positions are outside playbook. Several are on items the playbook treats as non-negotiable without principal approval.

| Area | Seller position | Playbook position | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m (start). 20% only as fallback with Amelia Frost's prior written authority | **Reject.** No authority has been given. |
| De minimis / basket (12.2) | AUD 25k de minimis; AUD 250k deductible basket | AUD 5k de minimis; AUD 50k tipping basket | **Reject.** Five times the de minimis and five times the basket, plus a deductible structure. |
| Time limits (12.3/13) | 18 months; limitations apply to all Claims unless stated | 24 months (18 months needs Amelia Frost approval); no hidden general-regime override | **Reject.** The "apply to all Claims" wording is a hidden override. |
| Fundamental / Title | Capacity and title subject to general caps and time limits | 100% cap, 6+ years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | **Reject outright.** |
| Limitations / exclusive remedy / non-reliance (9.3, 12.8, 20.5) | Apply to all Claims of any nature | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of everything, to the extent enforceable | **Reject.** No fraud carve-out. |
| Disclosure (Sch 7; DL 1.1, 1.2) | Whole data room, Accounts, statutory registers, public records | Specific fair disclosure only | **Reject.** |
| Buyer knowledge (8.3) | No claim for matters known or discoverable from the data room or public records | Delete blanket exclusion; qualifiers need named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | **Reject.** |
| Bluefen (3/6.3; DL 2) | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery; final consent not included | Effective consent and evidence of conditions before Completion; reasonable endeavours insufficient | **Reject.** Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue. |
| Riverlark (2/7; DL 3) | Release to be provided after Completion; AUD 3.2m still outstanding | Current payout; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective releases. Post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval | **Reject.** |
| Employee bonuses (funds flow; DL 5) | AUD 420k excluded from funds flow, "a matter for the Seller" | Specific line item or Seller-funded; not silently excluded | **Reject.** On-costs are also unquantified. |
| Ironquay IP (11.1; DL 4) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden the indemnity; preserve the SOW3 cure | **Reject as drafted.** |
| Export/privacy incident (4.6/Sch 6; DL 6) | "Not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach or numeric demand either way | **Do not accept the materiality view.** Obtain facts. |
| Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k) | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction | **Assess.** Do not accept the characterisation without evidence. |
| Tax / IP | "Settled under the general regime" | Remain OPEN; no unlimited liability assumed; no resolution | **Reject.** These are not settled. |
| Title (DD-012) | Share register evidences title | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence required; DD-012 is an internal source only | **Reject as sole evidence.** |

## Key Issues and Reasoning

**1. The Seller's general regime is materially weaker than our starting position.** The cap, de minimis, basket, deductible structure and time limit all move against us at once. Under the Seller's draft, a claim of AUD 100k would be worth nothing unless it cleared AUD 25k, and then only recovered above AUD 250k of aggregate claims. The 20% cap is only a conditional fallback in our playbook, and it requires written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft. None has been given. We should not signal acceptance of any of these figures.

**2. The "apply to all Claims" wording and the fundamental/title proposal are the most serious structural points.** The Seller is trying to pull title and capacity claims into the general regime and to make general limits apply across the board. Our playbook requires these to be separate. Under the Seller's draft, a title defect could be capped at AUD 4.8m and lost after 18 months. We should reject this and insist on a separate fundamental regime.

**3. Fraud is not carved out.** The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature" with no carve-out. This would expose us to being bound by the limitation on a claim for deliberate concealment. The playbook says no one may waive this carve-out, so this is a firm line.

**4. Disclosure and buyer knowledge together would hollow out our protection.** The Seller's general disclosure of the whole data room and public registers, combined with the buyer-knowledge exclusion for anything "discoverable", would mean we could be taken to know everything in a 20-plus-document data room. Read together, these would defeat most warranty claims. Both need to be deleted or replaced with specific disclosure.

**5. Bluefen is a condition, not a delivery item.** The Seller's own disclosure (DL 2) confirms no final written Bluefen consent and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied. Treating consent as satisfied on delivery of a counterparty letter is not what the playbook requires. We need effective consent and evidence the conditions are met before Completion. The reasonable endeavours wording is insufficient for a material customer consent.

**6. Riverlark is roughly AUD 3.2m that the Seller proposes to release after Completion.** The disclosure confirms the facility has not been repaid and the discharge is not included. Our playbook requires payout from Completion funds with effective security releases. A post-completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval. Without this, we could take the business subject to a bank security interest.

**7. The bonuses are a funds flow gap.** AUD 420k of conditional DD-005 bonuses are not in the funds flow, and the Seller describes them as "a matter for the Seller". Payroll tax and superannuation on-costs are not addressed at all. The playbook requires a specific line item or Seller funding, and the funds flow must not silently exclude them. We should also check whether the bonuses are triggered by Completion, which affects who should bear them.

**8. The Ironquay indemnity is too narrow.** The indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment, and DL 4 confirms no receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room. The AUD 180k figure in DD-010 is not independently verified. We should not assume it is right or wrong. Our position is to broaden the indemnity to cover IP transfer conditions and related costs, and to preserve the SOW3 cure (payment and confirmatory assignment). We should verify the balance with Ironquay and the bank.

**9. The export incident (DD-006) cannot be treated as immaterial yet.** The Seller calls it "not expected to be material", but the investigation is preliminary. The file may contain about 1,240 records with names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps. It is not known whether anyone accessed it, and whether notification is required has not been determined. Under the playbook, we should not assume a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. We should require preservation of logs, a completed investigation, regular updates and a view on whether Australian privacy notification obligations apply. Whether a specific indemnity is needed for the incident is a judgement call for the deal team; I would recommend raising it as a protective option.

**10. The Sandbar renewals need assessment, not automatic treatment.** The Seller says they are ordinary-course costs. The disclosure (DL 8) does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. The playbook requires assessment and no automatic debt classification or price deduction. We should request the contracts and renewal terms and decide the treatment on the evidence.

**11. Tax and IP are not settled.** The Seller's position that these are "settled under the general regime" is wrong on our playbook. They remain open. We should not accept any term that caps tax or IP at the general cap, and we should keep these categories separate.

**12. Title should not rest on the share register alone.** DD-012 is the Seller's supplied internal source, and the Seller's own disclosure (DL 10) says the Buyer has not verified title. We should require independent evidence: ASIC company extract, register of members verification, PPSR and other encumbrance searches, and evidence of authority.

**13. Consents not yet addressed.** The office lease (DD-007) notification obligation and the Mossvale assignment restriction (DD-009) were both disclosed without stating whether landlord or Mossvale consent is required for a share sale. These are not in the playbook but should be confirmed in writing before signing.

## Recommendations

**Reject in full and counter-propose:**
- General cap at 25% / AUD 6m, with no 20% fallback unless Amelia Frost gives written authority identifying this draft.
- De minimis AUD 5k; tipping basket AUD 50k; seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period of 24 months; 18 months only with Amelia Frost approval; no hidden general-regime override.
- Separate fundamental/title regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the extent enforceable.
- Specific fair disclosure only; delete whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Delete the blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion.

**Conditions and completion mechanics:**
- Bluefen: effective consent plus evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion. Reject reasonable endeavours and consent-on-delivery.
- Riverlark: current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases. Any post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
- Bonuses: AUD 420k as a specific funds-flow line item or Seller-funded, including quantified on-costs.

**Specific risks:**
- Ironquay: broaden the indemnity beyond SOW3. Preserve the SOW3 cure (payment and confirmatory assignment). Verify the AUD 180k balance independently.
- DD-006: preserve logs, complete the investigation, require regular updates, and obtain advice on whether any privacy notification applies. Do not accept the "not material" characterisation.
- Sandbar: request the contracts and assess. No automatic debt treatment or price deduction.
- Tax and IP: keep open. Do not accept settlement under the general regime.
- Title: independent ASIC, register, PPSR and authority evidence.
- Lease and Mossvale: written confirmation whether consent is required for the share sale.

**Next steps:**
1. Do not signal acceptance of any Seller position to the Seller's counsel.
2. Seek Amelia Frost's instructions on the 20% cap and the 18-month period, but only if the deal team wants to consider them. Neither has been authorised.
3. Prepare a mark-up of the SPA and disclosure letter reflecting the above.
4. Send the Seller a list of diligence requests covering the Bluefen conditions, the Riverlark payout, the Ironquay balance, the DD-006 investigation, the Sandbar contracts, title evidence, and the lease and Mossvale consents.
5. Have NSW counsel and, for DD-006, privacy counsel review the mark-up before it is sent.
